data.reasoningText:
I'm noticing the apply step doesn't re-verify allowed_branches—that check only happens in the MCP handler at call time—and the salt gets appended afterward, so a branch name like daily-playwright/2026-10-14 becomes daily-playwright/2026-10-14-<16hex>, which seems fine. I'm also looking at the fallback logic that generates a branch name from the workflow ID plus a random hex string when none is explicitly provided.

For Fix 3, I'm working out where to add the rule about patient routes: the coverage-scout's pass 2 should skip routes defined only in PatientRouter.tsx since they require a patient OTP session that no existing auth state provides. I think the scout filter is the right place for this, though adding a note in the authoring file's "Auth states" section could also help if the main agent later picks a patient-portal route from the tracker.

I'm also considering whether this rule needs to apply to tracker-carried-forward gaps too, since those come from pass 1 and might include stale patient routes — so the drop rule should probably be phrased generally enough to cover both freshly-scanned and tracker-sourced candidates. Now I want to verify exactly which routes exist only in PatientRouter versus ones shared with AppRouter or PublicRouter.

Next I'm looking at the safe-output guard for Phase 4, specifically how to prevent a run from completing with no PR and no noop call. I recall that in earlier testing, one model stopped entirely without emitting any safe output, so I need to make sure the instructions force either a PR or a noop every time, with the tracker entry always being recorded regardless.

I also need to handle the failure case in Phase 3 — if the agent can't produce a decent spec, step 11 should still ensure a tracker entry gets added with "PR: none — <reason>". I'll add a concise guard line at the start of Phase 4 stating every run must end with safe outputs: at minimum the tracker entry, plus the PR or noop — a run that ends in prose alone leaves no record. I'm also recalling that gh-aw likely detects when no safe outputs are produced and flags the run as incomplete.

For fix 5, CI triggering on bot PRs: the `github-token-for-extra-empty-commit` setting defaults to the `GH_AW_CI_TRIGGER_TOKEN` secret if present, so enabling CI just requires an admin to add that secret. I'll document this as a short frontmatter comment near create-pull-request, noting that PRs pushed with GITHUB_TOKEN don't trigger workflows and that adding a GH_AW_CI_TRIGGER_TOKEN secret (PAT or App token with contents: write) fixes it.

I'm second-guessing the "action_required with 0 jobs" detail though -- that state usually applies to first-time contributors needing run approval, but events from GITHUB_TOKEN normally don't create workflow runs at all except for workflow_dispatch/repository_dispatch, so I'm not fully certain why those runs appeared in that state for bot-created PRs.

With a GH_AW_CI_TRIGGER_TOKEN set, the empty commit gets pushed by that PAT/App identity instead, which counts as a trusted push and triggers CI automatically without needing manual approval. I want to phrase the comment carefully: pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN alone don't start CI, so Playwright runs wait for a maintainer's approval — but setting that secret makes gh-aw push an empty commit with it after opening the PR, which does trigger CI.

Now I'm checking whether the lock file actually references GH_AW_CI_TRIGGER_TOKEN to confirm no change is needed there. On the prettier/tsc pre-step question, I recall the lint CI only covers `./src`, so tests/ isn't checked by `npm run lint` or `npm run knip`, and prettier formatting is only enforced locally via husky pre-commit — so I need to figure out where the "prettier failures" on bot PRs were actually coming from.

Given the user deliberately skipped verification, adding a tsc pre-step feels low-value and would require installing node_modules in the agent job, slowing things down considerably — I'll flag it as an optional follow-up rather than implement it, since the reduced-error approach already relies on vendored authoring rules and sub-agent review rather than automated type-checking.

I'm also double-checking the temporary PR ID mechanism — referring to the PR as `aw_newpr` before it exists and letting the safe_outputs job replace it with the real number is valid gh-aw design, matching the required `aw_` prefix format for temporary IDs.

I'll verify the `temporary_id` format (`aw_newpr`) and the lock's `GH_AW_CI_TRIGGER_TOKEN` default before editing, since the rework depends on both.

arguments.command:
export GITHUB_REPOSITORY=ohcnetwork/care_fe; set -euo pipefail
gh pr list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --author "app/github-actions" \
  --search "head:daily-playwright/" --limit 100 --json number,title,body,files \
  --jq '[.[] | {number, title, target: ([.body | scan("(?m)^[-*]? ?Target: .+$")] | first), files: [.files[].path]}]' | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); [print(p["number"], "| target:", p["target"], "| files:", len(p["files"])) for p in d]'
tracker() {
  T="[daily-playwright] Coverage Tracker $1" gh issue list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state all \
    --author "app/github-actions" --search "\"Coverage Tracker $1\" in:title" --limit 10 \
    --json number,title,body,comments \
    --jq '[.[] | select(.title == env.T) | {number, title, body, entries: [.comments[] | select(.author.login == "github-actions") | .body]}]'
}
echo "--- tracker 2026-10:"; tracker 2026-10 | head -c 300; echo
echo "--- tracker 2026-09:"; tracker 2026-09 | head -c 300; echo
echo "--- existing tracker titles + comment authors (old format)"; for n in 16929 16869; do gh issue view $n --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json title,state,comments --jq '"#'$n' \(.state) \(.title) | comment authors: \([.comments[].author.login] | unique)"'; done

data.reasoningText:
The branch name pattern checks out as valid, and the token wiring is already in place. I'm confirming the snapshot step's search query works correctly, since the `head:` qualifier prefix matching was already verified with a successful search returning three results.

Combining `--author "app/github-actions"` with `--search` should work fine too.

Now examining the tracker JSON extraction more carefully: I'm checking the `jq` filter's behavior with `first` on an empty array, which correctly returns `null` as expected. But I'm flagging a potential issue with the `(?m)` regex flag in the scan expression — Oniguruma's Ruby-style regex syntax treats `(?m)` as dotall (making `.` match newlines) rather than multiline mode, since `^`/`$` are already line anchors by default in that syntax. This could mean the pattern greedily matches from "Target:" all the way to the end of the body instead of stopping at the line break, which would be a bug worth investigating further.

Good, this confirms it: in Oniguruma's Perl/Java syntax, `(?s)` makes dot match newlines while `(?m)` makes `^`/`$` match at line boundaries — opposite of Ruby syntax where `(?m)` means dotall. Since jq uses `ONIG_SYNTAX_PERL_NT`, it follows the Perl convention.

But I realize gh's `--jq` actually uses gojq, the Go implementation — not jq with Oniguruma at all. gojq relies on Go's RE2 regex engine, where `(?m)` enables multi-line mode for `^`/`$` anchors instead.

With RE2 semantics, the pattern should behave as intended, though I should consider that PR bodies might have `\r\n` line endings depending on whether they were authored via API or edited in the web UI, which could leave a trailing `\r` in the matched target — minor but worth noting. I'll verify the snapshot step's commands against the live repo to confirm behavior.

I want to check the `gh pr list` command with its filters and jq query, the tracker function using `env` (which gojq does support), and the comment-matching logic checking `author.login == "github-actions"` for bot-authored comments, since `set -euo pipefail` means any failure here kills the run before the agent even starts.

I should verify this against an actual tracker issue like #16929 or #16869 to confirm the login format. Also, since macOS uses BSD date which doesn't support `date -u -d`, I'll need to manually compute the previous month instead of relying on GNU date syntax, then test the commands locally with GITHUB_REPOSITORY set.

Confirmed `aw_newpr` matches the naming pattern and CI already references `GH_AW_CI_TRIGGER_TOKEN`, so only the secret is needed. Since the snapshot step runs under strict mode before the agent, I'll dry-run its queries read-only against the live repo using `gh`'s jq, as the step does.

I copied your rework into this worktree, committed it unchanged, fixed the remaining issues in a second commit, and removed the rework from your main checkout. Nothing is pushed yet.

- **Your rework, as-is (`9e6dccb30`):** the three files are byte-identical to what was in your main checkout.

- **Fixes (`78bf70dbe`):**
  - **Branch guard:** PRs must now come from a `daily-playwright/*` branch. Three past bot PRs (#16930, #16799, #16682) were on `develop-<hash>` branches, which hides them from the in-flight snapshot and the open-PR skip check. A wrong branch is now refused while the agent is still running, so it can correct itself. The prompt also tells it to create that branch before committing.
  - **Sub-agent model:** changed `small` to `claude-haiku-4.5`. For Copilot, gh-aw copies sub-agent settings verbatim and doesn't translate `small`.
  - **Patient routes:** the scout now skips routes that exist only in `PatientRouter.tsx`. They need a patient OTP login, and no test login state provides one.
  - **Always leave a record:** every run must end with at least the tracker entry, so it can't finish with only a text summary.
- **Checks:** the lock is recompiled and in sync with no warnings. The snapshot step's queries return the right results against the live repo.

**Correction to my earlier finding:** bot PRs aren't waiting for approval. Their Lint and Playwright runs are started by `github-actions[bot]` and fail with no jobs, so CI never actually runs on them. I added a comment in the workflow explaining the fix.

I didn't add a formatting/type-check step before the agent runs. It goes against your "skip verification" design, and Lint CI doesn't check formatting in `tests/` anyway.

**Needs an admin:**
- Add a `GH_AW_CI_TRIGGER_TOKEN` repo secret (a personal access token or App token). It isn't set at repo or org level, and it's what lets CI run on these PRs.
- Close the old trackers #16929 and #16869, and the failure issue #16918. The new monthly tracker won't close the old ones automatically.
